title: Scale the portions, not the pan
hook: A four-portion recipe uses 300g. How much corresponds to six portions?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Scale a recipe quantity while preserving quantity per portion.

misconception: The same ingredient quantity serves more people without changing portion size.
objective: Scale a recipe quantity while preserving quantity per portion.

claims.text: The quantity-only recipe uses 300g for four equal portions. Scaled model; quantities only; no cooking guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Portions=6, A=450g and B=300g. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",75,"x"]; B=300; x denotes Portions. At x=6, A=450, B=300; Transfer recall: A at x=10 gives 750g (300÷4×10). Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: The original rate is 75g per portion. Multiply that rate by the new portion count to keep the same amount per person. This demonstrates proportional quantity arithmetic, not cooking or nutritional advice.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",75,"x"]; B=300; x denotes Portions. At x=6, A=450, B=300; Transfer recall: A at x=10 gives 750g (300÷4×10). Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: A quantity-only recipe uses 300g for four equal portions. How many grams preserve that amount per portion for ten portions? Correct: 750g. 300g ÷ 4 = 75g per portion; 75g × 10 = 750g. Scaling the portion count scales the quantity by the same factor.
claims.source: Quantity-only arithmetic: 300g ÷ 4 portions = 75g/portion; 75g/portion × 10 portions = 750g. The recall asks for proportional quantity, not the unchanged comparison.

claims.text: Cooking times do not scale with quantity.
claims.source: Safety-required stage line (company/reviews/lh-scale-recipe-portions/2026-10-14-safety.md, lifehacks-safety-reviewer). Source owed: a food-safety body guidance, to be found and checked by the fact-checker. The reviewer named none, and none is asserted here.

recall.question: A quantity-only recipe uses 300g for four equal portions. How many grams preserve that amount per portion for ten portions?
recall.why: 300g ÷ 4 = 75g per portion; 75g × 10 = 750g. Scaling the portion count scales the quantity by the same factor.
